notes: EAST circled at the bottom of the sheet (entry / front side).
N. marked at the right-hand edge of the sheet.
10"x12" callout with a leader to the north-east corner; the green squares at the wall junctions are columns.
5" callout with a leader to the east exterior wall.
GATE drawn as a plain rectangle outside the south wall, directly below the main entrance door; it lies outside the 26' x 36' building envelope and is not modelled as a room.
ENGINEER SUBHASH written in highlighter in the middle of the plan (draughtsman's stamp, not a plan element).
A thin L-shaped line inside the Kitchen along its west and south sides is the kitchen platform / counter, not a wall.
UP arrow shown at the stair; no DN arrow is drawn.
'Stair' is written on the sketch beside 'Hall Room'; the Hall Room's written size 9'-7" x 11'-10" excludes the stair, so the stair is carried as its own zone.
assumptions: The written overall dimensions 26'-0" and 36'-0" are OUTSIDE-to-OUTSIDE, not centre-line. This is not stated on the sketch but is proved by the sketch's own figures: with every wall at the 5" thickness called out, 12'-5"+12'-4"+3x5" = 26'-0"; 8'-0"+9'-7"+4'-2"+3'-0"+3x5" = 26'-0"; 7'-6"+17'-3"+3x5" = 26'-0"; 11'-6"+4'-0"+7'-5"+11'-0"+5x5" = 36'-0"; and 11'-6"+11'-10"+11'-0"+4x5" = 36'-0". All five bands close exactly. Every coordinate in this file is built from that arithmetic.

Only one wall-thickness figure is written on the sketch (5", with a leader to the east exterior wall). 5" has therefore been applied to every wall, exterior and internal alike; the arithmetic above confirms it for all five bands.
The 10"x12" callout is a column size. Columns (the green squares at wall junctions) are not modelled as separate elements.

No door or window is dimensioned on the sketch. Every 'pos' and 'width' for openings was MEASURED off the image at a scale of about 42.5 px per foot, derived from the written 26'-0" overall width, and cross-checked against the 36'-0" overall height.
Interior single-door leaf arcs measured between 2'-10" and 3'-6"; they have been reported as 3'-0" each. The Bath+tat door measured about 2'-6" and is reported as such.

The main entrance door and the Hall-to-Drowing-Hall door are each drawn with TWO leaves and two arcs, and each measured about 4'-6" (over 1200), so both are double doors. Both are placed running from the east face of the Kitchen partition to the face of the column on the bedroom-partition line, which is where the sketch breaks the wall.

The Kitchen door's east jamb sits hard against the Kitchen partition, and the north-west BED ROOM door's east jamb and the north-east BED ROOM door's west jamb sit hard against the central bedroom partition. These positions are traced from the sketch, not centred.
Windows carry no numbers on the sketch - each is marked only 'W' (one is written 'W.'), so every window is tagged "W".

The highlighted strips on the east wall of the Drowing Hall Room, and on its south wall, are each read as TWO separate windows because a red tick divides the highlight. Each could alternatively be one long window with a mullion mark.
Window jamb positions and widths on the west, east, north and south walls were measured from the extent of the highlighter over the red wall.

The Dining has NO east wall drawn - it runs straight into the Hall Room. Its zone box is closed on the east at the line of the Bath+tat east wall purely as a zone boundary; no wall is listed there. Only its 7'-5" depth is written on the sketch; no width is written.
The stair's west edge is drawn as a thin black line, not as a red wall, so no wall is listed between the Hall Room and the stair - the stair mouth is open.

The stair is read as three flights and TWO landings, both labelled 'Landing' and both dimensioned 3'-0" square, hence type U3. Flight 1 runs east (treads drawn vertical) starting from the UP arrow on its west side; the turn is to the right (south) onto the middle flight down the east side (treads drawn horizontal); a second right turn leads onto the bottom flight running west.

Tread counts (7 / 9 / 7) were COUNTED off the sketch's drawn riser lines and are approximate - the lines are closely spaced and the sketch neither numbers its steps nor states a riser count. The 4'-2" figure dimensions the length of the outer flights and the 3'-0" figure the landings; these give roughly 7" per tread, which is smaller than a built tread, so the drawn line count may not be the intended number.

The bright highlighter bracket drawn on three sides of the space between the flights is taken as the stair well; no rectangle-with-an-X is drawn, and the well is open on its west side toward the Hall Room.
'Bath+tat 8' X 4'' is read as 8'-0" east-west by 4'-0" north-south; this is the orientation that closes the 36'-0" left-hand column.
No plan title is written on the sketch. It is taken as the GROUND FLOOR PLAN because the entry gate is drawn on it and the stair shows UP only.
North: 'EAST' is circled at the bottom of the sheet and 'N.' is marked at the right-hand edge, so north points to the right of the paper - north_deg = 0.
No railing, parapet, handrail, level mark, entry step, terrace, court, parking, planter or O.T.S is drawn anywhere on the sketch, so 'steps' is empty and no room is marked open_area.

The two bedrooms carry the identical name 'BED ROOM' on the sketch, so the swing.room reference for their two doors is identical; they must be told apart by position (the first listed is the north-west room, the second the north-east).
